$comment: AI workflows (decision 126): known processes as data. Read by backend/src/vaic/shared/workflows.py. A workflow is recognised in the owner's words (match.subjects; with match.actions it starts straight away, without them VAIC asks 'Is this what you mean'; match.not_when words mean it is something else, like a report). inputs are asked one at a time, in this order, only when missing; types: text, choice (options with words that mean them), money (an amount per day), date (start), end (a date, a number of days, or open), url. steps are the pages of the walkthrough: 'guide' is what the owner does by hand, 'do' is how the team does it through the connector; {key} is replaced with the owner's answer. spend names the inputs that make the money shown before anything is created. connector is a key of config/departments.json connectors; department is the preset that does the work. Add a workflow by adding an entry here; no code. Also: modes (default both), away_by_default (the owner is away unless they say they are here: inputs with a default are assumed, not asked, and become taste questions; nothing paid starts without a question), match.direct_only (only with an action word), input default and from_words (the owner's sentence is the answer), connector null (nothing outside the city), taste_topics (what the team asks the owner along the way with ask_taste, never waiting; decision 127).

workflows.name: Meta Ads campaign
workflows.summary: A Facebook and Instagram ad campaign, from goal to live ads.

inputs.label: Goal
inputs.question: What should the ads achieve, Sir: sales, leads, website visits or awareness?

inputs.label: What you advertise
inputs.question: What are you advertising? A product, a service or an offer, in a few words.

inputs.label: Landing page
inputs.question: Which web page should people land on when they tap the ad?

inputs.label: Who sees it
inputs.question: Who should see the ads: where they live, their ages and what they are into?

inputs.label: Images and videos
inputs.question: Should Marketing make the images and videos, or will you attach your own?

inputs.label: Daily budget
inputs.question: What's your daily budget?

inputs.label: Starts
inputs.question: When should the ads start?

inputs.label: Ends
inputs.question: When should they stop: a date, after a number of days, or keep running?

steps.title: Open Ads Manager
steps.guide: Open Meta Ads Manager (adsmanager.facebook.com), pick the ad account you pay from, and click + Create.
steps.do: Through the Meta Ads connector, list the owner's ad accounts and use the active one (if there are several and the owner named none, use the one with recent spend and say which).

steps.title: Pick the goal
steps.guide: Choose the objective {objective}. Name the campaign "{offer} - {objective}". If the ads are about housing, jobs, credit or politics, tick the special ad category.
steps.do: Create the campaign with the objective for {objective} (Sales = OUTCOME_SALES, Leads = OUTCOME_LEADS, Website visits = OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, Awareness = OUTCOME_AWARENESS), named "{offer} - {objective}", with any special ad category that applies declared.

steps.title: Budget and dates
steps.guide: In the ad set, set a daily budget of {daily_budget}. Schedule: start {start_date}, end {end_date}.
steps.do: One ad set with a daily budget of {daily_budget} (in the ad account's currency unless the owner named one), starting {start_date}, ending {end_date}.

steps.title: Who sees the ads
steps.guide: Set the audience: {audience}. Leave placements on Advantage+ (Facebook and Instagram).
steps.do: Target {audience}; Advantage+ placements on Facebook and Instagram; no overlapping ad sets.

steps.title: The ads
steps.guide: Create two or three ads that send people to {link}: images or videos ({creative}), a short headline, the main text about {offer}, and a button that fits the goal.
steps.do: Two or three ads pointing to {link} about {offer}: images and videos ({creative}; if the owner makes them, use the files they attached in the knowledge base, else have Design and Video & voice make 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 versions), headline, primary text and a call to action fitting {objective}.

steps.title: Check and publish
steps.guide: Check the summary, then click Publish. Meta reviews the ads, usually within a day, and they start on {start_date}.
steps.do: Check everything matches the owner's answers, then publish so it delivers from {start_date}: the owner approved exactly this budget and these dates in AI City, and their stated budget is the authorisation to spend it. Never raise the budget or add funds. Report the campaign, ad set and ad names and ids, and when results can first be read.

taste_topics: the ad's headline and its call-to-action button (Shop now, Learn more, Sign up)

workflows.name: Google Ads campaign
workflows.summary: A Google Search, Performance Max or YouTube campaign, from goal to live ads.

inputs.label: Goal
inputs.question: What should the ads achieve, Sir: sales, leads, website visits or awareness?

inputs.label: Campaign type
inputs.question: Where should the ads show: Google Search, everywhere on Google (Performance Max) or YouTube?

inputs.label: What you advertise
inputs.question: What are you advertising? A product, a service or an offer, in a few words.

inputs.label: Landing page
inputs.question: Which web page should people land on when they click the ad?

inputs.label: Who sees it
inputs.question: Where should the ads show, and what would your customers search for or be into?

inputs.label: Daily budget
inputs.question: What's your daily budget?

inputs.label: Starts
inputs.question: When should the ads start?

inputs.label: Ends
inputs.question: When should they stop: a date, after a number of days, or keep running?

steps.title: Open Google Ads
steps.guide: Open Google Ads (ads.google.com), pick the account you pay from, and click + New campaign.
steps.do: Through the Google Ads connector, list the owner's accessible customer accounts and use the active one (if there are several and the owner named none, use the one with recent spend and say which). Check conversion tracking for Sales or Leads and say so if it is missing.

steps.title: Goal and type
steps.guide: Choose the objective {objective} and the campaign type {campaign_type}. Name it "{offer} - {campaign_type}".
steps.do: Create a {campaign_type} campaign for the goal {objective}, named "{offer} - {campaign_type}".

steps.title: Budget and dates
steps.guide: Set an average daily budget of {daily_budget}, start {start_date}, end {end_date}. Bidding: maximise conversions for Sales or Leads, maximise clicks for visits.
steps.do: Average daily budget {daily_budget} (in the account's currency unless the owner named one), start {start_date}, end {end_date}; bidding that fits {objective}.

steps.title: Where and who
steps.guide: Set locations and languages, then keywords or audience signals from: {audience}.
steps.do: Locations, languages and, for Search, tightly themed ad groups with keywords and negatives (for Performance Max and YouTube, audience signals) from: {audience}.

steps.title: The ads
steps.guide: Write the ads that send people to {link}: for Search, 10 to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions about {offer}; for Performance Max or YouTube, add images and videos.
steps.do: Ads pointing to {link} about {offer}: responsive search ads with 10 to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions plus sitelinks and callouts for Search; images (1.91:1, 1:1, 4:5) and videos (16:9, 9:16) from Design and Video & voice for Performance Max or YouTube.

steps.title: Check and publish
steps.guide: Check the summary, then click Publish campaign. Google reviews the ads, usually within a day, and they start on {start_date}.
steps.do: Check everything matches the owner's answers, then enable the campaign so it serves from {start_date}: the owner approved exactly this budget and these dates in AI City, and their stated budget is the authorisation to spend it. Never raise the budget or change billing. Report the campaign, ad group and ad names and ids, and when results can first be read.

taste_topics: the headlines and the call to action
which image or video leads (Performance Max, YouTube)

workflows.name: App build
workflows.summary: A whole app built and finished by the team, from your idea to a working app under Projects.

inputs.label: The idea
inputs.question: What should the app do, in a sentence or two?

inputs.label: Who uses it
inputs.question: Who will use it: just you, your family or team, or your customers?

inputs.label: Must-have parts
inputs.default: The smallest version that does the idea well
inputs.question: Which screens or parts must it have?

inputs.label: Look
inputs.question: How should it look: clean and light, dark and sleek, or playful and colourful?

inputs.label: Paid or private
inputs.question: Does it take payments or keep accounts or private data?

steps.title: Plan
steps.guide: VAIC sums up what will be built: {idea}, for {users}, with {must_have}.
steps.do: Turn the idea into a short plan: {idea}, for {users}, must have {must_have}. Keep to what was asked; choose sensible simple defaults for anything unclear and note them.

steps.title: Build
steps.guide: The Apps team builds it: {look}, {paid_private}.
steps.do: Build it as a self-contained web app, look {look}; {paid_private} (anything paid or private follows the city's app rules). Ask taste questions as you go and never wait for the answers.

steps.title: Check
steps.guide: The manager checks every screen and action.
steps.do: Review every screen and key action against the plan; fix what fails, up to the usual review rounds.

steps.title: Publish
steps.guide: It appears under Projects once approved.
steps.do: Submit the finished app with submit_app so it is published under Projects (the Chief of Staff approves it while the owner is away). Report what was built, the defaults you chose and the taste questions you asked.

taste_topics: whether the owner likes a feature as built (keep, change or drop)
how one page should behave compared with another
the words on buttons and the main call to action
colours and layout of the main screen

workflows.name: Organic content
workflows.summary: Posts and short videos made by Media with your creative tools and published to YouTube, TikTok and Instagram, with no money spent.

inputs.label: The brief
inputs.question: What is the content about, in a sentence or two?

inputs.label: Where
inputs.question: Where should it go: YouTube, TikTok and Instagram, only short-video platforms, or only Instagram?

inputs.label: Format
inputs.question: What should it be: a short video, an image post or carousel, or a longer YouTube video?

inputs.label: Tone
inputs.question: What tone: friendly and clear, bold and energetic, or calm and expert?

steps.title: Plan
steps.guide: Media plans {format} about {brief} for {platforms}: the hook, the script and the caption per platform.
steps.do: Plan {format} about {brief} for {platforms}: search the knowledge base for the brand first, then write the hook, script or storyboard and a caption per platform (each platform's format and length). Choose sensible defaults and ask taste questions as you go; never wait.

steps.title: Make
steps.guide: The team makes it with your creative tools: Canva for designs, Higgsfield or EveryGen for video, ElevenLabs for the voice, draw.io for diagrams. Tone: {voice}.
steps.do: Make it with the creative connectors that are on (Canva for designs and thumbnails, Higgsfield, HeyGen or EveryGen for video, ElevenLabs for voice-over and sound, draw.io for diagrams), tone {voice}. Use only licensed music and the owner's own or generated material; label realistic AI content as the platforms require. If a tool is off, use the next one; never sign up for anything.

steps.title: Check
steps.guide: The manager checks it against the brand and each platform's rules.
steps.do: Review the result against the brief, the brand in the knowledge base and each platform's format; fix what fails.

steps.title: Publish
steps.guide: It is published to {platforms} through the accounts you connected.
steps.do: Publish it to {platforms} now, as organic posts (the owner's request is the go-ahead; no money is spent): through the platform's own connector when the owner added it (YouTube, TikTok or Instagram official API), otherwise the publishing tool that is on (Metricool, Buffer, Ayrshare or Blotato). Never boost, promote or spend: paid ads are a separate workflow with the owner's budget. If no publishing account is connected, save the finished files and captions to the knowledge base and say in one line which account to connect. Report the links.

taste_topics: the hook and the first seconds
the caption and call to action
